title: Pilot structured encampment shelter model endorsed in principle
subtitle: Zoning enforcement pause for the Italian Canadian Club patio, land inventory work, winter homelessness costs and federal funding requests.
overview: Council held a special meeting mainly to follow up on a temporary structured encampment for people experiencing homelessness. After hearing from health partners, a service provider, people with lived experience and the volunteer tiny homes coalition, and after a closed session, council endorsed in principle a pilot structured encampment shelter model {{vote:m5}}. Councillors changed the original wording from a tiny home model to a pilot structured encampment {{vote:m4}}. No site has been chosen.

Staff were directed to keep identifying City-owned or other lands that could host temporary or permanent housing and to report back by Q1 2025. Council also asked the County's Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee to bring winter 2024/25 housing costs to the September 24, 2024 council meeting. It asked the federal government for immediate funding allocation and criteria. A separate request asks the County's Housing and Health Community Planning Table to look at prioritizing people in encampments for health and housing supports {{vote:m6}}.

Earlier, council paused zoning enforcement on the Italian Canadian Club's outdoor patio at 135 Ferguson Street until October 1, 2024, provided a minor variance application arrives by August 13 {{vote:m1}}. After the closed session, the Mayor reported that council received information and gave no direction.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed in principle a pilot structured encampment shelter model and asked the County to consider how it fits the housing continuum, with staff to keep identifying City-owned or other land and report by Q1 2025 {{vote:m5}}.
Council replaced the reference to a tiny home shelter model with a pilot structured encampment shelter model {{vote:m4}}.

Council asked the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee to refer estimated costs of temporarily housing people from the by name list not placed elsewhere to the September 24, 2024 council meeting.
Council asked for immediate funding allocation and criteria for federal funds to address encampments and homelessness.
Council asked, through Wellington County, that the Housing and Health Community Planning Table investigate prioritizing health and housing supports for people living in encampments {{vote:m6}}.

Council paused enforcement of zoning provisions for the Italian Canadian Club's outdoor patio and parking removal until October 1, 2024, contingent on a minor variance application by August 13, 2024 {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Delegates from health and housing organizations and people with lived experience said more options are needed before winter, that shelters do not suit everyone, and that a smaller site with staff gives people secure space and easier access to services.

Councillors questioned what the model actually is: temporary or permanent, shelter or supportive housing, and what the rules on drug use would be. The coalition said it hopes the model is temporary but cannot predict, and that drug use would not be allowed in public areas.

Councillors raised funding concerns, noting the City does not usually fund operating costs for social services. The coalition said funding details can follow once council signals the model is a priority and a site is found. One councillor also asked why new supportive and transitional housing opening this fall would not be enough; delegates said there still would not be enough options.

Councillors and staff discussed how well the scope of homelessness is known. Delegates thought encampment numbers were higher than reported. Staff said numbers shift and the exact count matters less than coordinating agencies and getting people onto the by name list through the County's systems.

On the amendment, one councillor argued the County should not be asked to fit this model into the housing continuum, since the Kitchener delegate said it was built regardless. The mover kept the wording, noting that it says the model "may" fit.
